entries.title: SIKH EMPIRE: AV rupee (1/15 mohur), Multan, VS1905. NGC MS62
entries.description: SIKH EMPIRE: AV rupee (1/15 mohur), Multan, VS1905, KM-87, Herrli-11.09.04, struck by Diwan Mulraj during the British siege of Multan, NGC graded MS62.   The Siege of Multan was a prolonged event between the British East India Company and the city and state of Multan. The siege lasted from April 19, 1848, when a rebellion against a ruler installed by the East India Company started the Second Anglo-Sikh War, until January 22, 1849, when the last of the defenders surrendered.

entries.description: SIKH EMPIRE: AE paisa "pattern", 1830, KM-Pn1 (=X#1), Herrli-04-20-11, PCGS graded AU58.   Pseudo-Sikh machine-struck token or "pattern", also regarded as a fantasy, coarsely engraved Persian inscription on machine-struck planchet, citing Baba Nanak & Ranjit Singh, some original chocolate brown luster, with the usual die cracks frequently found on examples of this type, reeded edge.

entries.title: SIKH EMPIRE: AR mahmudshahi rupee (10.71g), Derajat, AH1233. VF
entries.description: SIKH EMPIRE: AR mahmudshahi rupee (10.71g), Derajat, AH1233, KM-373, Herrli-07.01.04var, countermarked on the Khanda symbol of the Sikhs on the reverse, thus authorizing the continued circulation of a normal Durrani rupee of Derajat after the Sikh takeover of Derajat in AH1236, choice VF, RRR.    The only other recorded Derajat mahmudshahi rupee with the Khanda countermark appeared in our Auction #22, Lot 946, which was dated AH1236, the year of the conquest. This piece verifies the theory that the Khanda was applied in order to keep the older mahmudshahis of Derajat in circulation, and thus prevent a critical coin shortage.
